key_insight: In thin 316L foil laser welding, keyhole instability at higher line energy triggers hole nucleation and rapid hole growth, which can progress from stable seams to perforation and cutting.
engineering_relevance: The results provide a practical process window and stability criterion for suppressing defects in overlap welding of ultra-thin sheets.
method: High-speed imaging tracked keyhole behavior during laser bead-on-plate welding of 200 μm foils representing 100 μm overlap sheets.
Line energy was varied to map the transition from continuous seams to hole formation and cutting.
A Young–Laplace-based force balance was used to interpret hole growth from melt-pool curvature and surface tension.
evidence_signal: Continuous seams were achieved up to about 7 kJ/m, holes appeared beyond this range, and cutting dominated above about 12 kJ/m, with holes expanding at roughly 0.8–1.2 m/s over 1–3 ms.
watch_item: The proposed stability criterion is geometry- and thickness-dependent, so it may need re-parameterization for different alloys, sheet thicknesses, or joint configurations.
paper_title: Rupture and growth of holes in the melt pool during laser keyhole welding of thin sheets
